chunks: And the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, said:
"The one who washes the deceased is the person closest to him, or one whom the guardian instructs to do that."

key_terms.أَوْلَى: having the strongest priority or greatest entitlement
key_terms.النَّاسِ: the people in relation to the deceased
key_terms.الْمَيِّتَ: the deceased person whose body is to be washed
key_terms.الْوَلِيُّ: the guardian or authorized relative with legal authority in this matter
key_terms.بِذَلِكَ: for that task or act mentioned
key_terms.يَغْسِلُ: performs the ritual washing of the deceased

ai.seo_question: Who should wash the deceased in Shia Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning who is entitled to perform the ghusl of the deceased. It establishes priority for the closest rightful person, while also permitting the wali to appoint someone else for the task.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.391 - The Commander of the Faithful Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) said:
"The one who washes the deceased should be the closest person to them or the one whom the guardian (Wali) of the deceased appoints for this task."
